To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel approach to identify p 53 target genes has identified the vitamin D receptor as a p 53 target, that p 53 induces the vitamin D receptor in a vitamin D -dependent manner, and that p 53 induction of the vitamin D receptor results in the induction of other p 53 target gene s and the suppression of tumor cell growth.
the vitamin D receptor is a direct transcriptional target of p53 and that vitamin D3 induces the expression of p53 target gene(s) via VDR.
a comparative genomics strategy was used to identify novel p53-responsive genes and that p53 directly regulates VDR, which has a role in tumor cell growth and chemoprevention.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new p53 target genes using a comparative genomic approach.
the molecular mechanisms of tumor suppression by the tumor suppressor gene, p53.
the identification of novel p53 target gene and the role of p73 and p63 in the regulation of p53 gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vitamin D receptor is a novel p53 target gene that is involved in the regulation of p53 target gene expression.

the VDR is a direct transcriptional target of p53 and p63 and that the induction of the VDR by p53 and other p53 family proteins may be an important mechanism by which these proteins exert their tumor suppressive effects.
the VDR gene is a novel direct p53 target gene that may contribute to p53-mediated tumor suppression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the p53 protein is able to induce VDR expression in a p53 binding sequence dependent manner.
p53 is a transcriptional co-activator for VDR gene expression.
the VDR gene is a direct p53 target, and p53-induced VDR is an important component of p53-mediated tumorigenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the VDR gene is a direct target of transcriptional activation by p53 and that p53-induced VDR expression may be an important component of the antiproliferative effects of p53.
the p53 tumor suppressor protein is a transcriptional co-activator that binds directly to DNA to induce transcription.
the p53 protein binds the intronic sequences of VDR in vivo, and that the VDR protein can be a novel target for the p53 protein in cancer cells.
